questions.q: Why does this lesson argue the migration isn't actually finished until it's documented?
options: Because Azure requires documentation before a resource group can be billed
Because right now only Theo knows how everything is configured, and that knowledge needs to be written down so someone else could operate or troubleshoot it if Theo isn't available
Because documentation is a formality with no real operational purpose
Because the quiz for this lesson requires it
questions.explain: A migration that only lives in one person's head isn't done -- it's undocumented risk with a deadline attached, especially right before a launch.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the "known limitations" section in the runbook?
options: To list every feature Azure offers that wasn't used
To explicitly restate the project's scope -- one VM, no auto-scaling, no CI/CD -- so nobody assumes capabilities that were never built
To document bugs found during Lesson 7's testing
It has no real purpose and could be safely skipped
questions.explain: Restating the Lesson 2 scope in the runbook prevents a teammate from assuming the system can do something -- like auto-scale -- that it was deliberately never built to do.

questions.q: Why does "what the alert watches, and who it notifies" need to be documented, even though the alert rule already exists in Azure?
options: It doesn't need documenting -- the alert rule is self-explanatory from the email alone
So an on-call teammate who receives the 2 a.m. notification knows exactly what triggered it and what it means, without having to guess or dig through Azure configuration under pressure
Azure deletes alert rule configurations after 30 days
Documentation is required before an Action Group can send email
questions.explain: Someone reacting to a real alert at 2 a.m. needs the context already written down, not buried in a configuration they'd have to reverse-engineer under pressure.

questions.q: Why should the runbook be written before Lesson 9's cutover presentation, rather than after?
options: Because Priya explicitly forbids presenting without documentation
Because a presentation built on documentation that doesn't exist yet has nothing real to reference, and "write it up after launch" is exactly when nobody has time to
Because Azure requires documentation to exist before a VM can go live
There's no real reason -- the order doesn't matter
questions.explain: Writing the runbook first means the cutover plan can point to something real and already written, instead of promising documentation that will likely never get written under launch-week pressure.

questions.q: What should a resource inventory table include for this project?
options: Only the VM's name, since it's the most important resource
The resource group, storage account, blob container and tier, VM name and size, Log Analytics workspace, alert rule, and Action Group -- what exists and where, in one place
A full copy of every Azure CLI command run during the project
Only resources that cost money, excluding free ones like the Activity Log
questions.explain: A resource inventory table should answer "what exists and where" in one scannable place, covering every resource created for the project.
